name: Ingraham Direct

pitch_detail.notes: 4,600 ft up the Muir Snowfield; non-glaciated but weather-exposed
rope up; cross the Cowlitz Glacier to the gap
flat crevassed bench; route diverges here from the Cleaver
climb directly up the headwall past the bergschrund, under the icefall — the crux and the hazard
weave through crevasses to the southeast crater rim

descent_text: From the crater rim descend the upper glacier and traverse onto the Disappointment Cleaver, following it down to the Ingraham Flats, then Cathedral Gap and the Cowlitz to Camp Muir; from Muir, plunge-step or glissade the Muir Snowfield to Paradise. Stay roped across all glaciated terrain. Reversing the steep Ingraham headwall is possible early when it is firm, but most parties prefer the Cleaver for the descent.
approach: The Ingraham Direct on Mount Rainier begins at Paradise (5,400 ft). Follow the paved Skyline Trail through subalpine meadows and past Panorama Point (~5-7 hours) to Camp Muir (10,080 ft), gaining about 4,700 ft. Above Camp Muir, traverse the heavily crevassed Ingraham Glacier—rope-team travel mandatory. A hard overnight freeze is essential for safe glacier travel; start the summit push at 1-2 AM to climb the final 3,400 ft while snow is firm. Non-technical but exposed; the crux is route-finding through crevasse fields and steep snowfield sections.
overview: The Ingraham Direct is the early-season twin of the Disappointment Cleaver, climbing straight up the Ingraham Glacier headwall beneath the Ingraham icefall instead of detouring onto the Cleaver's rock rib. It's usually in best shape from winter through May while the headwall is still filled and continuous; NPS climbing rangers steer parties onto the Disappointment Cleaver once the bergschrund opens and rockfall/icefall exposure from the serac band above increases.
beta: Ascends the Ingraham Glacier headwall directly, weaving among crevasses (a switchback boot path usually lowers the effective angle to 35-40°); a prominent crevasse called 'High Crack' near 11,200 ft regularly requires a ladder crossing even early season, and large seracs near 12,500 ft on the west side of the glacier are avoided by cutting east above the Cleaver.
gear: Rope, harness, and a full crevasse-rescue kit (pulley, prusiks) for the Ingraham Glacier crossing
4-6 pickets of your own — roughly a dozen fixed pickets are typically already placed along the route, but personal rope-team spacing still needs its own anchors
2-3 ice screws — current route updates specifically recommend screws because the lower route has been running firm and icy rather than soft snow
Helmet, for icefall/rockfall exposure below the Ingraham Icefall and Cathedral Rocks
fa: Unknown (Rainier was first climbed August 17, 1870 by Hazard Stevens and P.B. Van Trump, via Gibraltar Ledges)
